name: Report images and pages
summary: How to build a report, as a static image (a PNG for Slack, email or an export) or as a read-only report page a report routine publishes, so both forms look the same: size and density, type, series order and the top 3 plus Other rule, end labels, twin-axis legends, gaps, notes on real zero runs, tick density and number formats, titles, missing glyphs, and the report table and number plate looks.
highlights: The DS chart rules, plus what a still image cannot do
Report tables: zebra rows, in an image and on a report page alike
Number plates and KPI tiles: Vivid Pink at 5% card, black text, pink top bar, as many as the report needs
Status glyphs: lib/static-icons in an image, <aha-icon> on a page, never drawn
lead: A report comes in two forms that look the same. A report image is a chart, table, number plate or KPI tile rendered once to a PNG and posted to Slack, an email or an export. A report page is a read-only page (a dashboard) that a report routine publishes: people open it from a link to read it, and never operate it. Both follow the same rules as the live DS elements (<aha-chart>, <aha-stat-tile>, the colour rules), and colour rule 3.11 gives both their colour: zebra table rows and pale pink number plates. One difference drives the image rules: nobody can hover, zoom or read a tooltip on an image, so every value a reader needs is written on it and every glyph is a file from the DS, because a renderer that cannot run <aha-icon> cannot draw one either. A screen of the product app, including its Report screens, is not a report page: it keeps plain table rows and white tiles.

skillRef.note: The DS owns this ruleset. A report page builds with the live elements <aha-chart> (contracts/chart.json) and <aha-stat-tile look="accent"> (contracts/stat-tile.json); a report image copies them, with the static glyphs from lib/static-icons (build-static-icons.mjs); the judge criteria and evals live in anti-slop/.

Vivid Pink: the 2px table header rule, the plate top bar and the first chart series

rules.rule: An image is drawn at 2x: a full-width chart is 1,200 by 675 px at 1x and exported at 2,400 by 1,350. Keep text at least 12 px at 1x (ticks, notes) and 14 px for labels and values, a 24 px margin on a white background, one chart, table or plate row per image, and the file under 1 MB so Slack shows the preview. A report page is a white page that reflows from a 360 px phone up with no horizontal scroll, the same text sizes, and as many charts, tables and plate rows as the report needs.
Plus Jakarta Sans only, from the bundled font files, in two weights: 400 for ticks, captions, notes and table text; 600 for titles, values, end labels and table headers.

Colour series in the chart order (Vivid Pink, black, Vivid Pink at 30%, light grey #A8A8A8), the main series first. A breakdown with more than four parts shows the top three by value and folds the rest into Other, in light grey and last. Never more than four colours.

Every line carries its latest value at its right end, formatted like its axis. Labels never overlap: when two would touch, push them apart and join each to its line with a short leader in the series colour. A series in Vivid Pink at 30% or grey is always labelled (colour rule 8.3).

Add a right axis only when a series has a different unit (a rate beside a count). Both axes share the grid lines, and the legend names each series' axis: Sessions (left axis), Conversion (right axis).
A missing period breaks the line. Never draw it as zero and never join across it; a point with no neighbour keeps its marker so it still shows.

When a series is really zero for three or more periods in a row (not missing), add a short note on the chart in secondary text, such as No sessions from 3 to 9 Oct, so the flat run is not read as missing data.

Use 3 to 6 y-axis divisions on round steps, starting at zero for counts. Thin the x labels until none overlap, counting back from the latest period so it is always labelled. Write 1,000 and above as K or M with at most one decimal (12K, 1.3M), percentages as whole numbers (46%), and use the same format on the axis, the labels and any table.

Titles are sentence case and say what and when (Weekly sign-ups, last 12 weeks). No em or en dashes anywhere on the image: use a comma, or to for a range (3 to 9 Oct). No full stop at the end of a title.

Every character renders. Set a fallback font that covers every script the data can hold (Noto Sans for Vietnamese and other diacritics), so a name never turns into empty boxes; draw arrows and status marks from lib/static-icons, never from font characters or emoji.

A table in a report, image or page, has zebra rows alternating white and Vivid Pink at 5% (#FEF3F7) with the 1px row dividers kept, header labels in black semibold over a 2px Vivid Pink rule, figures in black tabular numerals aligned right and text aligned left, and no vertical rules or status colours. This is colour rule 3.11 and applies to reports only: a table on a screen of the product app keeps plain rows, because people work in it with a hover highlight; a report is read, not worked in.

A number plate (the KPI tile) is a flat card in Vivid Pink at 5% with a 4px Vivid Pink top bar and 8px corners: the label in black 400, the value in black 600, the change as an absolute number and a whole percent, then the comparison caption in secondary text. A rise is black with the up arrow; a fall is white on a black pill with the down arrow. No green, red or other status colour, and no shadow. On a report page it is <aha-stat-tile look="accent">, as many as the report needs; in an image it is drawn to the same spec. Colour rule 3.11 allows the pale pink card in both.

Status marks are DS glyphs called by their registry names (system-arrow-up, system-arrow-down, system-warning-circle, system-hourglass-high …) at 12, 16, 24 or 32 px, in ink or white: <aha-icon> on a report page, the SVG files in lib/static-icons in an image. Never draw a triangle, a circle or an emoji in their place.

selfCheck.label: image: 2x export, text at least 12 px at 1x, white background, under 1 MB; page: reflows from 360 px with no horizontal scroll
Plus Jakarta Sans 400 and 600 only; fallback font for missing glyphs
series in the chart order; top 3 plus Other past four parts
end labels on every line, never overlapping; gaps break the line; zero runs carry a note
twin axis named in the legend; 3 to 6 round divisions; K, M and whole % formats
sentence-case titles with no em or en dashes
tables, in an image and on a page: zebra white and #FEF3F7, dividers, black semibold header over a 2px Vivid Pink rule
plates: Vivid Pink at 5% card (<aha-stat-tile look="accent"> on a page), pink top bar, black text, rise and fall by shape; glyphs from the DS

reuseNote: Doc-only guideline. A report page uses the live elements <aha-chart> and <aha-stat-tile look="accent">; a report image copies them, with the static glyphs that ship as files in lib/static-icons, generated by build-static-icons.mjs and checked by its test.
